newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SEOUL STOCKS CLOSE HIGHER, 750 BARRIER BREAKS.
newsitem.headline: SEOUL STOCKS CLOSE HIGHER, 750 BARRIER BREAKS.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed up on Friday, breaking the psychological barrier of 750 points with the help of institutional buying of blue chip issues, brokers said.
They said the bullish sentiment would likely continue into Saturday's half session, but that a consolidation should be expected in the near future.
The composite stock index closed up 6.66 points to 752.01 with 33.99 million shares changing hands.
"The market needs some sort of consolidation before taking off again," said Kim Wan-hee of Dongsuh Securities.
Among the favoured blue chips, Pohang Iron and Steel was the star performer, rising 1,700 won to 60,600.
Korea Electric Power gained 600 to 27,400 and Hyundai Motor added 700 to 25,200.

"We won't see a big jump in blue chips tomorrow but possibly a steady rise," said Lim Chong-woo of Ssangyong Investment Securities. "Institutions, taking a positive view of the market, are accumulating blue chips."
Brokers said most of Kia Group shares surged to their upper daily limit in late afternoon on a rumour that the chairman of the troubled group would resign.
Kia Motors rose 1,000 won to 14,000, Kia Steel added 250 to 3,420, Asia Motors gained 360 to 4,860, Kisan climbed 380 to 5,180 and Kia Motor Sales rose 370 to 5,090.
Kia Precision, was the only Kia share not closing at its limit high. It rose 710 to 10,500.
"There is a rumour in the market that Kia's chairman would resign soon," said Park Joo-chang of Daewoo Securities.
"Investors believe the group could be normalised with the supply of emergency funds."
Kia creditors have promised to extend emergency loans to the group if its top executives tender resignation letters.
Brokers said it was uncertain how the Kia shares would perform on Saturday. But every development would closely be monitored.
"It's really hard to say because Kia shares have fluctuated widely every day on different rumours," said Lim of Ssangyong.
Ssangyong Motors soared in afternoon on a news report that its German partner Daimler-Benz Ag was evaluating the automaker's assets prior to a stake hike.
Confirmation of the report was not immediately available.
Ssangyong rose 360 won to its upper limit of 4,980.
Brokers said the report could keep the shares firm for another day.
Daimler-Benz has confirmed that it is in discussions with Ssangyong but not that it would increase its stake in the Korean company.

Small- to medium-priced stocks with prospects of improved first-half earnings also caught interest, brokers said. Korea Tungsten, an integrated mining, smelting and manufacturing company, added 1,300 won to its limit high of 17,600.
